item.text: {"search_note":"Direct 2024 evidence on outcomes for education quality, learning, primary healthcare performance, and administrative throughput is thinner than the evidence on budgets and new programs.\nThe strongest positive items are often government self-reports or budget allocations, not independent outcome evaluations.\nThe clearest negative evidence is on regulatory predictability and service pressure from inflation, not on a total absence of spending.","evidence":[{"title":"India plans to spend $134 billion on infrastructure, narrow fiscal gap - interim budget","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-02-01","url":"https://theprint.in/india/india-plans-to-spend-134-billion-on-infrastructure-narrow-fiscal-gap-interim-budget/1948810/","summary":"The interim budget raised infrastructure spending to a record level, increased education and health outlays, and kept the fiscal deficit on a tightening path. This is strong evidence that Modi’s government invested in core productivity foundations rather than pure short-term giveaways.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.1","5B.3","5B.4"]},{"title":"India's Modi promises to create jobs, boost infrastructure if BJP wins third term","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-04-14","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-promises-to-create-jobs-boost-infrastructure-if-bjp-wins-third-term/2040266/","summary":"Modi’s manifesto explicitly tied growth to jobs, infrastructure, semiconductors, green energy, aviation, railways, and expanded health coverage for seniors. This is a direct campaign pledge to invest in productivity-enabling sectors.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.1","5B.4"]},{"title":"India's Modi plans post-election reforms to rival Chinese manufacturing","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-06-03","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-plans-post-election-reforms-to-rival-chinese-manufacturing/2113220/","summary":"Modi planned business-friendly reforms such as easier hiring/firing rules and lower input taxes to improve manufacturing competitiveness. This supports a pro-productivity, pro-regulation-reform reading, though it is still only a plan.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4"]},{"title":"With renewed focus on next generation administrative reforms the Government has approved an outlay of Rs. 235.10 crore","publisher":"Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions","date":"2024-01-18","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1997326&lang=2&reg=48","summary":"The government approved funding for AI-assisted grievance redress, service delivery, process re-engineering, and capacity-building in administrative systems. This is direct evidence of investment in administrative capacity.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4"]},{"title":"100 days of Modi 3.0: Ambitious reforms in Healthcare and Education for a Resilient Future","publisher":"Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare","date":"2024-09-28","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153215&lang=1&reg=3","summary":"The first 100 days of Modi’s third term featured health and education measures including expanded Ayushman Bharat coverage for seniors, U-WIN, new medical seats, and digital health/medical registries. This is positive evidence for human-capital investment, though it is official self-reporting.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.1","5B.4"]},{"title":"Update on Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission","publisher":"Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare","date":"2024-12-17","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2085201&lang=2&reg=48","summary":"ABDM had built large-scale digital health infrastructure, including ABHA accounts, facility registries, professional registries, and linked health records. This is strong evidence of technology investment for more transparent and scalable health delivery.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4"]},{"title":"Cabinet approves the Digital Agriculture Mission today with an outlay of Rs. 2817 Crore","publisher":"Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare","date":"2024-09-02","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2050966&lang=2&reg=48","summary":"The government approved a Digital Agriculture Mission built around digital public infrastructure, crop estimation, and data-driven agricultural support. This is direct evidence of technology investment aimed at productivity gains in a major sector.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4"]},{"title":"India's Modi faces delicate balancing act in post-election budget","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-07-23","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-faces-delicate-balancing-act-in-post-election-budget/2186495/","summary":"The post-election budget tried to combine fiscal prudence with spending on jobs, rural programs, and long-term infrastructure, but was also explicitly shaped by coalition pressure and voter management. This is positive on investment foundations, but mixed on predictability and pure technocratic planning.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5"]},{"title":"India's high food inflation leaves less in lunch boxes of poor school children","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-10-10","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/indias-high-food-inflation-leaves-less-in-lunch-boxes-of-poor-school-children-3659018","summary":"School meal budgets had not kept pace with food inflation, forcing cutbacks in nutrition for poor children. This is counterevidence that productivity foundations, especially education and child health, were fully protected in practice.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.1"]},{"title":"India | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","date":"2024-06-17","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/india","summary":"The report highlights broad new regulatory powers, concerns about the fact-check unit, the Telecommunications Act, and government access/surveillance powers. This is negative evidence for predictable regulation, because the state was expanding its discretion in ways critics saw as opaque and overbroad.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.5"]}]}
